title: Characterization of Some Selected Silica Sand Deposits in South West Nigeria for Sand Moulding in Foundry Industry
abstract: This study determined the clay content, chemical composition, grain fineness number, distribution and shape of silica-sand deposits from Igbokoda, Ote, Opa and Osooro in south-west Nigeria for foundry moulding. XRF/XRD showed quartz dominance and silica contents of 80.56–86.46%; all deposits were classified grade D.
authors: Omotajo Adewole Adeyemi; Omotola Tobilola Emmanuel; Olawale J. Olawale; Isadare Dayo A.; Adetunji A. R.; Adekoya O.; Adeyemo O.
venue: Nigerian Journal of Materials Science and Engineering
african_relevance: Nigeria; South West Nigeria; local_mineral; local_manufacturing

title: Effect of Compactive Effort on the Geotechnical Properties of Metakaolin Treated Black Cotton Soil
abstract: The study examined black cotton soil treated with up to 10% metakaolin from calcined kaolin under British Standard Light, West Africa Standard and British Standard Heavy compaction. Treatment reduced liquid and plastic limits and lowered hydraulic conductivity; the authors recommended the material as a liner or cover for waste-containment facilities.
authors: T. S. Ijimdiya; G. Imam; T. Igboro; A. Tanko
venue: Nigerian Journal of Materials Science and Engineering

title: Moulding Properties of As-Mined and Silica-Enriched Potters’ Clay
abstract: Ipetumodu potters’ clay was dried, ground, sieved and mixed with 5% water, then tested for green/dry compression, green/dry shear strength and permeability. Clay–silica mixtures were evaluated and compared with foundry moulding sand used at the Federal Institute of Industrial Research, Oshodi.
authors: S. A. Ibitoye; A. A. Afonja
venue: Journal of Construction and Materials Technology

title: Testing of Cement Stabilized Lateritic Soil Using Various Indirect Tensile Strength Test Methods
abstract: Brazilian split-cylinder, double-punch, flexural-beam, non-Brazilian point-load and ring tensile tests were applied to cement-stabilized soils containing 0–8% cement. Results were analysed graphically and with brittleness models to compare the tensile-test methods.
authors: F. C. Emesiobi; F. O. Aitsebaomo
venue: Journal of Construction and Materials Technology

title: Mix Design Optimization of High-Performance Concrete Using Local Materials
abstract: Twelve concrete mixes made from local materials were evaluated using water–cement ratios of 0.30, 0.35 and 0.40 and different coarse-aggregate size combinations. Workability and compressive, flexural and tensile strengths were tested through 90 days; predictive strength models were proposed.
authors: Efe E. Ikponmwosa; Kolawole A. Olonade; Abdulgafar O. Sulaiman; Emmanuel O. Akintunde; Numeri O. Enikanologbon; Olusegun A. Kehinde
venue: Nigerian Journal of Technology
african_relevance: Nigeria; University of Lagos; local_material; local_conditions

title: Compressive, Bending and Shear Properties of Reinforced Concrete Beams Containing Sawdust Ash as Partial Replacement of Cement
abstract: Concrete cubes and reinforced concrete beams containing 0–10% sawdust ash as cement replacement were cured and tested through 180 days. A 5% ash replacement achieved the required compressive strength and met structural-concrete requirements.
authors: O. E. Osanyinlokun; C. A. Fapohunda; O. M. Olaniyan
venue: Nigerian Journal of Technology

title: Reliability Evaluation of Compaction Water Content of Plantain Peel Ash Treated Lateritic Soil
abstract: FORM was employed to assess optimum moisture content of residual lateritic soil mixed with plantain peel ash and compacted with British Standard Light and Heavy energies for flexible-pavement applications.
authors: K. Ishola; O. A. Olawuyi; P. Yohanna; A. A. Bello; R. O. Sani; O. Akin
venue: Nigerian Journal of Technological Development

title: Mechanical Properties of Millet Husk Ash Bitumen Stabilized Soil Block
abstract: This study investigates strength and durability improvement of lateritic soil blocks using millet husk ash and bitumen, aiming to reduce cost and provide an agricultural-waste outlet. Selected blends achieved high compressive strength and watertight bricks.
authors: M. T. Abdulwahab; O. A. U. Uche; G. Suleiman
venue: Nigerian Journal of Technological Development

title: Investigation of the Properties of Concrete Made with Fly-Ash and Dry Waste Okra Powder
abstract: The research investigates fly ash and dry waste okra powder in concrete. Ten percent of cement was replaced with fly ash and 0.25–1% dry waste okra powder was added; selected blends produced higher strengths than the control.
authors: Y. Rahmat; A. S. Abdulazeez; I. Gambo; I. Audu; A. A. Isah
venue: Arid Zone Journal of Engineering, Technology and Environment

title: Effects of Rice Husk Ash on Durability of Self-Compacting Concrete Made with Cassava Peel Ash
abstract: This study evaluates durability of self-compacting concrete made with cassava peel ash combined with rice husk ash at 5–25% cement replacement. The ashes improved acid and sulfate resistance and reduced water absorption.
authors: M. T. Abdulwahab; O. A. U. Uche; A. Aboshio; A. Mohammed; A. Suleiman; A. M. Auwal; S. U. Chidawa
venue: Arid Zone Journal of Engineering, Technology and Environment

title: Geotechnical Properties of Lateritic Soil Stabilized with Banana Leaves Ash
abstract: Lateritic soil collected at the Federal University of Technology, Akure, Nigeria was tested after adding 2–10% banana-leaf ash. The ash improved soil strength and unsoaked CBR reached an optimum at 4% ash.
authors: Emeka Segun Nnochiri; Olufikayo Aderinlewo
venue: FUOYE Journal of Engineering and Technology

title: Effects of Sesame Straw Ash as a Substitute for Cement on Strength Characteristics of Concrete
abstract: This study recycles sesame straw ash as a cement substitute in greener concrete. Replacement levels of 0–25% were tested; concrete with 10% ash exceeded the design strength at 28 days.
authors: Tasiu A. Sulaiman; Stephen P. Ejeh; Adamu Lawan; Jibrin M. Kaura
venue: FUOYE Journal of Engineering and Technology

title: Assessment of Compressive Strength of Concrete Produced with Fine Aggregate from Different Locations in Kaduna State
abstract: This research examined engineering properties of fine aggregate used in concrete works in Kaduna State and assessed how aggregate source affects concrete compressive strength.
authors: Uwemedimo Nyong Wilson; Izzideen Balarabe; O. C. Eze; Abdullahi Adefila; M. A. Adole
venue: FUTA Journal of Engineering and Engineering Technology

title: Enhancing Asphalt Pavement Performance through Palm Kernel Shells Integration
abstract: The study evaluates locally available palm kernel shells as an asphalt-mixture modifier to improve pavement performance, addressing waste reuse and road-material needs in Nigeria.
authors: O. S. Aderinola; G. O. Ata
venue: FUTA Journal of Engineering and Engineering Technology

title: Differential Maturity across Lateritic Profiles from Ilorin, North Central Nigeria
abstract: This study characterizes upper crustal, middle gravelly and basal lateritic horizons near Ilorin using geotechnical tests. The gravelly middle horizon exhibited the highest maturity and expected engineering performance.
authors: O. A. Odediran
venue: LAUTECH Journal of Engineering and Technology

title: Influence of Elastobar and Zycoprime Nanochemicals on Concrete Properties with Coarse Aggregate Partially Replaced by Periwinkle Shell
abstract: This study tests concrete containing periwinkle shells collected from Ilaje, Lagos State as partial coarse-aggregate replacement, with Elastobar and Zycoprime additives, and evaluates grading and strength properties.
authors: Destiny Ogenetega Jackson; Olatunji Sunday Olaniyan; Kingsley Obinna Obilor
venue: LAUTECH Journal of Engineering and Technology

title: Rock Characteristics and Ball Mill Energy Requirements at Goldfields Ghana Limited, Tarkwa Gold Mine (TGM)
abstract: Goldfields Ghana Tarkwa Mine ores were characterized and compared with plant design parameters. Work index differed from design and simulation identified a suitable throughput for the required energy draw.
authors: Charles Ebenezer Abbey; Kenneth Joseph Bansah; Greg Galecki; Kofi Agyeman Boateng
venue: Ghana Mining Journal
african_relevance: Ghana; Tarkwa Gold Mine; local_gold_ore; mineral_processing

title: Characterisation of Small-Scale Gold Mining Tailings in the Western Region of Ghana
abstract: Artisanal small-scale gold mining tailings from five Ghanaian locations were assessed by size analysis, gold grade and deportment, and cyanidation, informing reprocessing of Ghanaian ASGM tailings.
authors: I. J. Cobbinah; G. M. K. Gbedemah; Z. K. Nurudeen; A. K. Saim; R. K. Amankwah
venue: Ghana Mining Journal

title: Optimising Blend Ratios, Grinds, and Reagent Schemes to Recover Platinum Group Metals from Lower Group Reef Spiral Tailings
abstract: Lower Group chromite spiral tailings from a South African chrome mine were blended and tested with flotation, grind and reagent changes to develop a practical PGM recovery route.
authors: T. L. Moodley; I. Govender; S. Pikinini; J. Sehata; J. Tshilongo; M. Raedani
venue: Journal of the Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
african_relevance: South Africa; Bushveld Igneous Complex; Lower Group chromitite; PGM_tailings

title: Characterisation of the Reworked Residual Norite in the Rustenburg Region of South Africa
abstract: Twenty-six samples of reworked residual norite underlying tailings facilities in South Africa Rustenburg region were characterized using index and strength testing to assess tailings-storage stability.
authors: E. Zannoni; T. Grobler; G. Heymann
venue: Journal of the Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
african_relevance: South Africa; Rustenburg; Bushveld Igneous Complex; tailings_storage_foundation
